newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares recover, hit new record closing level.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares recover, hit new record closing level.

text.p: Danish share prices clawed back on Tuesday losses occured after last Friday's warning to markets by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan, going on to close at a new all-time record high with dealers seeing more gains ahead.

"We are being pushed on the U.S. It looks like Wall Street is going to rise today after the Dow Jones got off to a good start, so we can expect more U.S.-inspired gains on the stock market here tomorrow," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.74 point or 1.33 percent higher at a record closing 132.34, 0.60 point above last Thursday's close before Greenspan sent prices tumbling.
The previous all-time KFX index record closing high was last Thursday's 131.74.

The KFX December future rose 2.45 point to 132.10 with 330 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded. All KFX shares apart from SAS and NKT climbed handsomely, with B&O closing 22 crowns up at 267 after forecasting 25 percent higher half-year 1996/97 pre-tax profits.
Novo Nordisk steamed on, putting on 30 crowns to finish at 1130, but Tele Danmark was the day's most traded paper with 263,000 shares changing hands to close six crowns up at 301.
Overall turnover for the day was 970 million crowns.
